q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of wooden toys, such as Channapatna toys?
title: Wooden toys carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the wood, lac or lacquer colours, varnish and packaging per kg of toys, then lathe and drying energy. Divide by kilograms sold. Turned wooden toys use little fossil energy per kg; wood carbon is reported separately, and colours and packaging can be a large share.
audience: Wooden toy makers and handicraft exporters

ul: Wood such as hale or rubberwood: count wood bought, including turning waste.
Lac, natural or synthetic colours, varnish.
Cartons, tissue and labels; export packing can outweigh small toys.
Lathe motors, often small and many.

p: Report per kg and per piece for each product line. If artisans work at home on their own lathes, ask for their electricity units or estimate from motor ratings and hours, and label the estimate.

example.title: Worked example: toy unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 2,130 / 4,000 = 0.532 kg CO2 per kg
Add wood, lac, colours and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
